The entry point also exports everything `@canvist/web` does, every extension, and `allExtensions`. - `editor.caretRectAt(position)` is where a caret at `position` is drawn, in document coordinates, or `null` when the document has no such position or it isn't laid out. Hosts draw other people's carets with it; the collaboration guide shows how. - `@canvist/headless/extras` exports the extensions beyond the StarterKit and `allExtensions` on their own, without a WebAssembly module. - `canvist_web` has a `full` feature: every extension, the emoji table, and the layout for tables, ink, kinetic text, and the theme's blocks and marks beyond the StarterKit. #### Add `@canvist/web`, the canvas editor for the browser, with a fonts plugin _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #137](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/137) - `@canvist/web` and `canvist_web` paint the document on an opaque Canvas2D context with HiDPI backing stores, dirty-rectangle repaints, and baselines and backgrounds snapped to the browser's own pixel grid. `createEditor` types commands, queries, and plugin APIs from what you register. - Text is measured by the browser: `measureText` advances with kerning placed as shapers place it, line boxes read from the DOM, family lists resolved to the face the DOM uses, and DOM ranges for Arabic and for Firefox's fractional sizes. The canvas wraps where server-rendered HTML does. - `@canvist/web/fonts` loads faces from URLs or bytes with `unicode-range` and `font-display`, builds metric-compatible fallbacks, lists local fonts through `queryLocalFonts`, and writes the same faces as `@font-face` CSS for SSR. - `canvist_layout`: `TextMeasurer` batches carry line-box requests that a measurer may answer; `DocumentLayout::forget_fonts` relays out only the blocks a loaded face affects; `measure_stats`, `line_ranges`, `fonts`, and `font_metrics`; kerning between adjacent segments; `chromium_breaks`; border widths snapped to device pixels; `Theme::starter_kit_with` for dark and custom-font themes, and `Chrome::background`. `to_html` now sets the background and `text-spacing-trim: normal`, the StarterKit code stack no longer names `ui-monospace`, and graphemes come from the editor's segmenter. `ParleyMeasurer` sets a variable font's optical size to the font size, as browsers do. - `canvist_headless`: `Doc::edit` runs editor calls with a host's clock and line navigator, and `Doc::command_named` resolves a named command. - `@canvist/headless` exports its generated extension descriptors at `@canvist/headless/extensions`, with no WebAssembly. ### 🐛 Fixed - **Move the repository to canvist/canvist.** canvist now lives at [github.com/canvist/canvist](https://github.com/canvist/canvist). Every repository, documentation, and badge link points there, the npm packages declare their repository, homepage, and issue tracker (with support@canvist.dev), and the release workflows run for the `canvist` organisation. The website footer has a Contact link to support@canvist.dev. _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #148](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/148) #### Screen readers meet the text field first, and placeholders have 4.5:1 contrast _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #168](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/168) - In Firefox and Safari, where text arrives through a hidden textarea, the textarea now sits right after the canvas, as EditContext's field does in Chromium, so screen readers reach the editor's text field before its document mirror. - The placeholder shows the body text's colour at 62% instead of 50%, which gives 4.5:1 contrast on the StarterKit's light and dark pages. - New browser tests: an axe audit (WCAG 2.2 AA) of editable, read-only, empty, and menu-showing editors; virtual screen reader smoke tests; and Safari composition, Android keyboard, and touch input sequences in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. #### Keep `@canvist/web` lean when it compiles only the StarterKit _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #179](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/179) `@canvist/web` compiles the StarterKit alone. It now carries no code for extensions its schema cannot reach: - Clipboard codecs and StarterKit theme rules for extension blocks and marks compile only with their features. - Table grids, ink drawings, and kinetic motion compile only with `canvist_layout`'s `tables`, `ink`, and `kinetic` features. Layout's hot paths read a row's grid part through accessors that are always `None` without `tables`. - The editor builds its extension metadata the first time it is read, not on every build. The browser editor never reads it. Across the extension layers, its bundle budget in `tools/bench/size.json` moves from 350,000 to 359,000 gzipped bytes, and its wasm budget from 340,000 to 345,000, for engine growth every host shares: - JSON object and list values in attributes and command arguments. - List and record argument types. - The clipboard core's new block and mark handling. - Extensions vetoing updates, `can()` dry runs, and editor settings. - Text alignment and direction in layout. #### Fit the web editor in its 350 KB budget _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #137](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/137) - `@canvist/web` now ships 349.8 KB gzipped, measured as an app bundles it (`npm run size`, enforced in CI). The WebAssembly module is optimized without inlining, which gzips smaller. - `canvist_layout::css_number` formats CSS numbers without `core`'s float formatting, which no longer links into the module. - `EditorState::change` and `InputRule::new` keep one copy of their logic instead of one per command and rule, and `Engine::metadata` is built on first use.
📖 Documentation - **Mark the browser platforms Available.** The web, React, Vue, server-side rendering, and design canvas quick starts, the platform tables in the readme and the docs, the agent guide and skill, and the website's platform list now say "Available". The package readmes describe read-only editors, placeholders, menus, collaboration, server rendering, and the bundle budget. _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #173](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/173)
⚡ Performance #### Add text alignment, typography, character count, and placeholders _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #159](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/159) Four editing extensions beyond the StarterKit, each behind its own Cargo feature in `canvist_extensions` and part of `full`: - `TextAlign`: a `textAlign` attribute on paragraphs and headings, with `setTextAlign`, `toggleTextAlign`, `unsetTextAlign`, a `textAlign` query, and `Mod-Shift-l`, `e`, `r`, and `j`. HTML reads and writes TipTap's `style="text-align: …"`. - `Typography`: TipTap's 22 smart punctuation rules plus Remirror's `<->`, configurable with `without` and `with_output`. Rules that end in a digit fire on the space or punctuation after them. - `CharacterCount`: `characters` (grapheme clusters), `words`, and `characterLimit` queries, and `setCharacterLimit`. Edits that would go past the limit don't apply. - `Placeholder`: hint text for empty blocks, with TipTap's `showOnlyCurrent` and `includeChildren`, a `placeholder` query, and `setPlaceholder`. `canvist_extensions::extras()` lists every extension beyond the StarterKit with its default configuration. Supporting changes: - `canvist_core`: - `Extension::update_filters` lets an extension refuse a local update after its fix-ups, like TipTap's `filterTransaction`. The update is undone, the command reports that it did not apply, and `Editor::can` answers the same way. The filters are collected when the editor is built, so an editor whose extensions have none pays nothing per update. - `EditorState::settings`, `EditorTransaction::set_setting`, and `commands::set_setting` keep per-editor values such as a limit or placeholder text outside the document, its history, and collaboration. Dry runs restore them. - Extension metadata now lists only the nodes the built schema has. - `InputRule::on` names the typed characters that can complete a rule whose pattern ends in a group or class, so it doesn't run on every punctuation keystroke. - Input rules no longer panic when their 64-byte look-back starts inside a multi-byte character, which `**bold**` after a line of `€` or CJK text could trigger. - `canvist_layout`: - Lines align to a block's `textAlign` attribute: left, centre, right, or justified by widening spaces. Server-rendered HTML writes the matching `text-align`. - A row now rereads its `dir` and `textAlign` attributes when the block changes. Before, changing `dir` kept the old direction until the row was rebuilt. - `DisplayOptions::placeholder` draws placeholder text, faded, in an empty block. - Clipboard: pasted block attributes keep only the ones the block type declares. The `@canvist/web` bundle budget moves to 354,000 gzipped bytes, for update vetoes, editor settings, `can()` dry runs, and text alignment, which every host runs. #### Add subscript, superscript, highlight, and TipTap's text style kit _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #155](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/155) canvist's first extensions beyond TipTap's StarterKit, each behind its own Cargo feature in `canvist_extensions` (`full` enables every one), with TipTap's JSON names, commands, and keys: - `Subscript` (`Mod-,`) and `Superscript` (`Mod-.`), which exclude each other. - `Highlight`: `==text==`, `Mod-Shift-h`, and a `color` attribute (multicolour by default; `Highlight { multicolor: false }` matches TipTap's default). - `TextStyle` with `Color`, `BackgroundColor`, `FontFamily`, `FontSize`, and `LineHeight`, which each add one attribute to the `textStyle` mark, with set and unset commands and a query for the shared value. Supporting changes: - `canvist_model`: `SchemaBuilder::block_attrs` and `mark_attrs` add attributes to types other extensions register, like TipTap's global attributes. `MarkSpec::excludes_registered` excludes marks only when the schema has them. `EmbedSpec::attrs` sets an embed's defaults. - `canvist_core`: `commands::update_mark_attrs` rewrites one mark's attributes run by run, keeping each run's others. - `canvist_layout`: `TextStyle::baseline_shift` and `TextPatch::baseline_shift` raise or lower text like CSS `vertical-align`, in canvas layout and server-rendered HTML alike. `AttrBinding::LineHeight` reads a mark's line height. The StarterKit theme styles `subscript`, `superscript`, and `textStyle.backgroundColor` and `lineHeight`. `TextStyle` has a new public field, so code that builds one literally must set `baseline_shift`. - Clipboard formats: HTML reads and writes ``, ``, ``, and ``; Markdown writes `==text==` and GitHub's `` and `` tags and reads them back. Pasted marks keep only the attributes their type declares. - `canvist_headless`: the `full` feature registers every extension by name in `Engine::named`, which `canvist_headless_wasm` and the Dart bridge enable. The browser editor still compiles the StarterKit only. `Engine::named` now registers names in one fixed order whatever order they are given in, so the same names always build the same schema and every binding nests and serializes marks alike. - `@canvist/headless/full` and the Dart `canvist` package export a typed descriptor and handle for each new extension, generated from the new full metadata snapshot. `allExtensions` (TypeScript) and `Extensions.starterKit` (Dart) list them; `starterKit` is unchanged. - Conformance fixtures can list `extensions` to add to the StarterKit, and every runner supports them. The StarterKit theme's rules for blocks, marks, and embeds beyond the StarterKit sit behind a new `canvist_layout` feature, `theme-extensions`. `canvist_canvas`, `canvist_canvas_wasm`, and `canvist_paint` turn it on. `@canvist/web` builds without it, and its bundle budget moves to 352,000 gzipped bytes for the engine growth every host shares. #### Add mentions, hashtags, and emoji on a shared suggestion system _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #166](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/166) Three extensions, each behind its own Cargo feature and part of `full`, share one suggestion engine, like TipTap's Suggestion utility and Remirror's suggesters. Typing `@`, `#`, or `:` after a space starts a suggestion. A `…Suggestion` query reports `{ char, query }`, a command replaces the trigger with the pick and a space, and Escape or a dismiss command hides it until the trigger is typed again. - `Mention`: TipTap's `mention` embed with `id`, `label`, and `mentionSuggestionChar`, plus `insertMention`, `dismissMentionSuggestion`, and `mentionSuggestion`. Backspace after a mention turns it back into its trigger. - `Hashtag`: a `hashtag` mark with a `tag`, marked as you type and paste, with `insertHashtag`, `dismissHashtagSuggestion`, `hashtagSuggestion`, and a `hashtags` list query. - `Emoji`: TipTap's `emoji` embed with `name`, plus canvist's `emoji` attribute holding the character. It covers GitHub's 1,870 gemoji, `:shortcode:` as you type, `setEmoji`, `dismissEmojiSuggestion`, `emojiSuggestion`, and `searchEmoji({ query, limit })`. Supporting changes: - `canvist_model`: `Value::Map` holds nested attributes. JSON objects in attributes become maps instead of `null`, and they round-trip. - `canvist_core`: `ValueType::List` and `ValueType::Record` describe structured query answers. Bindings generate typed lists and records from them. - `canvist_collab`: maps in attributes travel through Yjs instead of being dropped. - `canvist_layout`: `EmbedStyle::Label` gains a `fallback` attribute, drawn when the label's attribute is missing: after the prefix, or as `:value:` without one. The StarterKit theme draws an emoji without its character as `:name:` and a mention without a label as `@id`, as every export does. Code that builds a `Label` literally must set `fallback`. - `canvist_headless`: query and command arguments accept JSON objects. - Clipboard: HTML reads and writes TipTap's mention and emoji spans and canvist's hashtag spans. A mention without a label reads back without one. Plain text and Markdown write what a mention or emoji shows. - `@canvist/headless` types list and record answers. The Dart `canvist` package answers with typed records, such as `({String char, String query})`, and its queries take arguments. The `@canvist/web` bundle budget moves to 356,000 gzipped bytes and its wasm budget to 342,000, for JSON object and list values and list and record argument types, which every host runs. The StarterKit theme's mention rule moves behind `canvist_layout`'s `theme-extensions` feature, beside the emoji rule, so hosts that compile only the StarterKit, such as `@canvist/web`, carry neither. The Dart package's Flutter editor views turn on `canvist_layout`'s `theme-extensions` feature, so they style the extensions the package ships. #### Add tables _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #177](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/177) `Table` (feature `table`, included in `full`) is TipTap's TableKit. It adds a `table` of `tableRow`s holding `tableCell`s and `tableHeader`s, each cell holding blocks, with TipTap's `colspan`, `rowspan`, and `colwidth` attributes. - **Commands:** - `insertTable`; - `addColumnBefore`, `addColumnAfter`, `deleteColumn`; - `addRowBefore`, `addRowAfter`, `deleteRow`; - `deleteTable`, `mergeCells`, `splitCell`, `mergeOrSplit`; - `toggleHeaderRow`, `toggleHeaderColumn`, `toggleHeaderCell`; - `setCellAttribute`, `goToNextCell`, `goToPreviousCell`, `fixTables`. - **Query:** `tableCell` returns where the selection head sits, with its spans and the table's size. - **Selections:** a selection from one cell to another selects the rectangle of cells between them. - **Keys:** Tab moves to the next cell and adds a row past the last. Backspace and Delete never join text across a cell's edge, and deleting a selection across cells clears them. - **Headers:** toggling the header row or column leaves the corner cell to the other one when it is on, as TipTap does, so toggling twice changes nothing. - **Repairs:** short rows are padded with empty cells after every structural change, including a gap left of a cell that spans down from the row above. `canvist_model` adds `TableMap`, which places a table's cells on its grid from their spans. Layout places tables on a grid: - Columns take their `colwidth`, or an even share of what is left. - Each row is as tall as its tallest cell, and spanning cells grow their last row. - Grid lines are drawn as CSS's collapsed borders. - Hit testing, arrow keys, incremental relayout, and splicing all follow the grid. - A keystroke in a table of 1,000 cells relays out in about 7 µs. The HTML renderer writes a fixed-layout `` with the same column widths, and gives header cells a `scope`: `col` across the first row and `row` down the first column. The StarterKit theme draws hairlines and tints header cells. HTML reads and writes `
` as TipTap does, including bare text in cells and a row that a merged cell spans entirely. Markdown writes a GitHub pipe table when the table fits one exactly, and HTML when it does not. It reads both back, with column alignment. Grid layout sits behind a new default `canvist_layout` feature, `tables`, which `canvist_canvas`, `canvist_canvas_wasm`, and `canvist_paint` turn on. `canvist_web` builds without it, and the `@canvist/web` bundle budget moves to 357,000 gzipped bytes and its wasm budget to 343,000, for the grid hooks every host carries. - **Drop metadata descriptions from the browser editor's module.** `@canvist/web` builds its WebAssembly module with `--cfg canvist_omit_docs`, which leaves the command, query, and argument descriptions out of `canvist_core`'s metadata. Only bindings that generate types read them, and the browser module never does. With `wasm-opt --converge`, the editor ships 349.1 KB gzipped, down from 349.97 KB, under its 350 KB budget. _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #154](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/154)
🔨 Refactor #### Render documents on JavaScript servers with `@canvist/headless/ssr` _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #154](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/154) `@canvist/headless/ssr` renders a document as semantic HTML and a stylesheet laid out exactly as `@canvist/web` paints it, so a page shows the text before any JavaScript runs and the live editor hydrates from it without moving a pixel. It works in Node, Deno, Bun, and Workers, and so in Next.js server components and Nuxt server routes. ```ts import { createRenderer } from "@canvist/headless/ssr"; const renderer = await createRenderer({ theme: { bodyFamily: "Inter, sans-serif" }, }); const { html, css } = renderer.html({ format: "markdown", input: "# Hello" }, { width: 640, }); ``` - `renderer.html(content, { width })` returns `{ html, css }`, `renderer.page(content, { width })` a complete page, and `renderer.svg(content, { width })` an SVG image for previews. Content is text in a format or ProseMirror JSON, the same `Content` type `@canvist/web` takes. - `createRenderer({ extensions, theme, fonts })` takes the browser editor's extensions and `ThemeOptions`, and font files for SVG text. `registerFont(bytes)` adds one later. - Rendering is a third WebAssembly module, `wasm-ssr/`, so the document entry point stays small. - `ThemeOptions` and `Content` are now exported by `@canvist/headless`, and `@canvist/web` re-exports them. - `canvist_layout` gains a `json` feature with `StarterKitOptions::from_json`, which reads the theme options as both packages pass them. `canvist_headless`'s `ssr` feature enables it and re-exports `canvist_layout`. - The `ssr_page` Rust example is gone: `examples/web` now renders its server-rendered pages with `@canvist/headless/ssr` on each request, including a React page rendered with `renderToString` and hydrated with `hydrateRoot`.

sections.title: 🚀 Feature
entries:
#### Add details, callouts, and math

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #175](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/175)

Three block extensions, each behind its own Cargo feature and included in `full`:

- `Details` (`details`): TipTap's `details` block, holding a `detailsSummary` and a `detailsContent`, with an `open` attribute. Use `setDetails`, `unsetDetails`, `toggleDetailsOpen`, and the `detailsOpen` query. Enter in a summary opens the details and moves into the content; Backspace at the start of a summary unwraps the details, and no edit leaves a details without its summary or content. Layout draws a closed one as its summary beside a `▸` disclosure marker and lays out none of the hidden content.
- `Callout` (`callout`): Remirror's tinted box, with a `type` of `info`, `warning`, `error`, `success`, or `blank`. Use `toggleCallout`, `setCalloutType`, and the `calloutType` query. Typing `:::warning` at the start of a line makes one, and the StarterKit theme colours each type.
- `Mathematics` (`mathematics`): TipTap's `inlineMath` embed and `blockMath` block, holding LaTeX in `latex`. Use `insertInlineMath` and `insertBlockMath`, or type `$$x^2$$` and `$$$x^2$$$`. Layout draws inline LaTeX as its source and reserves a slot for block formulas, so the host can typeset them.

HTML reads and writes TipTap's markup:

- `<details>` with a `<summary>` and `<div data-type="detailsContent">`;
- `<div data-callout-type>`;
- `<span data-type="inline-math">` and `<div data-type="block-math">`, with the source in `data-latex`.

Markdown writes callouts as GitHub alerts (`> [!WARNING]`), details as GitHub's `<details>` HTML, and formulas as `$x$` and `$$` blocks, and reads all three back. A price such as `$5` stays text.

Server-rendered HTML marks a callout as a `role="note"` labelled with its type, which otherwise only its colour shows, and a block formula as `role="math"` labelled with its LaTeX.

#### Add ink drawings and kinetic type, drawn by the canvas itself

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #179](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/179)

Two canvas-native extensions, each behind its own Cargo feature and included in `full`.

**`Ink` (`ink`)** adds `ink` blocks: freehand drawings in a space 1000 units wide and `height` units tall, scaled with their column.

- Strokes are `points` lists of `x, y` pairs with an optional `color` and `width`.
- Commands: `insertInk`, `addInkStroke`, `undoInkStroke`, and `clearInk`. Query: `inks`.
- Each stroke is one undo step and one Yjs update.
- HTML writes a `<figure data-type="ink" role="img" aria-label="Drawing">` with an SVG of the drawing and the strokes as JSON. Markdown writes the same HTML, and both read it back.

**`Kinetic` (`kinetic`)** adds the `kinetic` mark, whose `effect` is `wave`, `shake`, `pulse`, or `rainbow`.

- Commands: `setKinetic`, `toggleKinetic` (another effect switches to it), and `unsetKinetic`. Query: `kineticEffect`.
- HTML writes `<span data-kinetic="…">`. Markdown keeps the text.

`canvist_layout`:

- `DisplayItem::Stroke` is new, and the SVG renderer, `canvist_web`'s Canvas2D painter, and `canvist_paint` draw it with round caps and joins. A stroke holds a range of the new `DisplayList::points`, read with `DisplayList::stroke_points`, and its bounds, so no item but a text run owns memory and lists of text stay as fast to build as before.
- `LeafStyle::Ink` lays out drawings. `Motion` and `AttrBinding::Motion` set how text moves.
- `DisplayOptions::time` moves kinetic text glyph by glyph, and `DisplayList::animated` says when a later frame would differ. Without a time, text is still, as it should be for readers who prefer reduced motion.
- The HTML renderer draws ink as inline SVG in a figure named as an image, and animates kinetic text with CSS, off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- New default features `ink` and `kinetic` hold this code. `canvist_web` builds without them, as it does without `tables`.

`canvist_core`: `ValueType::sample` gives lists two items, so lists of pairs get valid samples.

`canvist_canvas` and `canvist_canvas_wasm` turn on `canvist_layout`'s new `ink` and `kinetic` features.

#### Add editor views, server rendering, and key platforms to the Dart package

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #152](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/152)

- `doc.view(measurer)` returns an `EditorView`: incremental layout of the document, a display list per frame (`frame`, which returns no display when nothing changed), keys, typing, IME composition, the text an input method edits, pointer and handle selection, clipboard formats, typed commands with wall-clock undo grouping, caret and selection geometry, and accessibility text. It shares the document, so commands run on the `Doc` and collaborators' updates reach the layout too.
- `TextMeasurer` is the host's half of layout: Rust calls it synchronously, once per relayout batch, through a `NativeCallable`. `FixedMeasurer` gives predictable layout for tests and servers. A measurer that throws fails the view call that needed it.
- `doc.toHtml(width)`, `doc.toSvg(width)`, and `doc.serverDisplay(width)` render on the server, as the editor lays out.
- `EngineBuilder.build` and `Engine.starterKit` take a `KeyPlatform`, so `Mod` is Cmd on Apple devices.
- Budgets for a keystroke through a view to its next frame (250 µs at 10,000 paragraphs, measured at about 65 µs) and an unchanged frame.

#### Report an engine's key platform and keep shared undo in the shared history

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #167](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/167)

- `Engine.platform` says which platform's key bindings an engine follows.
- An `EditorView` on a shared document sends `Mod-z`, `Mod-Shift-z`, `Mod-y`, and the `undo` and `redo` commands through the shared history, so undo never reverts a collaborator's changes.
- `EditorView.caretRect` and `selectionEnds` lay out the blocks they need, so a host can scroll to a caret far outside the viewport.

#### Add find and replace, a table of contents, comments, block moves, and clear formatting

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #178](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/178)

Five document tools, each behind its own Cargo feature and included in `full`:

- **`FindAndReplace` (`findAndReplace`).** `setSearchTerm`, `setCaseSensitive`, `nextSearchResult`, `previousSearchResult`, `replace`, `replaceAll`, and the `searchResults` query.
  - The term lives in the editor's settings, outside the document and its history.
  - Matching ignores case unless asked not to.
  - `replaceAll` is one undo step.
- **`TableOfContents` (`tableOfContents`).** The `tableOfContents` query lists headings with their level, text, outline number, and the one the selection is under. `goToHeading` moves the caret to one.
- **`Comments` (`comments`).** A `comment` mark whose `threads` attribute lists thread ids, so comments can overlap.
  - Commands: `setComment` and `unsetComment`. Queries: `activeComments` and `comments`.
  - HTML writes `<span data-type="comment" data-threads="…">`.
  - The StarterKit theme tints commented text.
- **`DragHandle` (`dragHandle`).** `moveBlockUp` and `moveBlockDown` (Alt-↑ and Alt-↓), and `moveBlocksTo` for drops. They move the blocks a text or block selection covers, such as a selected horizontal rule. A block alone in its container moves its container.
- **`ClearFormatting` (`clearFormatting`).** `unsetAllMarks`, `clearNodes` (paragraphs, lifted out of quotes and lists), and `clearFormatting` on `Mod-\`.

#### Add text alignment, typography, character count, and placeholders

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #159](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/159)

Four editing extensions beyond the StarterKit, each behind its own Cargo feature in `canvist_extensions` and part of `full`:

- `TextAlign`: a `textAlign` attribute on paragraphs and headings, with `setTextAlign`, `toggleTextAlign`, `unsetTextAlign`, a `textAlign` query, and `Mod-Shift-l`, `e`, `r`, and `j`. HTML reads and writes TipTap's `style="text-align: …"`.
- `Typography`: TipTap's 22 smart punctuation rules plus Remirror's `<->`, configurable with `without` and `with_output`. Rules that end in a digit fire on the space or punctuation after them.
- `CharacterCount`: `characters` (grapheme clusters), `words`, and `characterLimit` queries, and `setCharacterLimit`. Edits that would go past the limit don't apply.
- `Placeholder`: hint text for empty blocks, with TipTap's `showOnlyCurrent` and `includeChildren`, a `placeholder` query, and `setPlaceholder`.

`canvist_extensions::extras()` lists every extension beyond the StarterKit with its default configuration.

Supporting changes:

- `canvist_core`:
  - `Extension::update_filters` lets an extension refuse a local update after its fix-ups, like TipTap's `filterTransaction`. The update is undone, the command reports that it did not apply, and `Editor::can` answers the same way. The filters are collected when the editor is built, so an editor whose extensions have none pays nothing per update.
  - `EditorState::settings`, `EditorTransaction::set_setting`, and `commands::set_setting` keep per-editor values such as a limit or placeholder text outside the document, its history, and collaboration. Dry runs restore them.
  - Extension metadata now lists only the nodes the built schema has.
  - `InputRule::on` names the typed characters that can complete a rule whose pattern ends in a group or class, so it doesn't run on every punctuation keystroke.
  - Input rules no longer panic when their 64-byte look-back starts inside a multi-byte character, which `**bold**` after a line of `€` or CJK text could trigger.
- `canvist_layout`:
  - Lines align to a block's `textAlign` attribute: left, centre, right, or justified by widening spaces. Server-rendered HTML writes the matching `text-align`.
  - A row now rereads its `dir` and `textAlign` attributes when the block changes. Before, changing `dir` kept the old direction until the row was rebuilt.
  - `DisplayOptions::placeholder` draws placeholder text, faded, in an empty block.
- Clipboard: pasted block attributes keep only the ones the block type declares.

The `@canvist/web` bundle budget moves to 354,000 gzipped bytes, for update vetoes, editor settings, `can()` dry runs, and text alignment, which every host runs.

#### Add subscript, superscript, highlight, and TipTap's text style kit

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #155](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/155)

canvist's first extensions beyond TipTap's StarterKit, each behind its own Cargo feature in `canvist_extensions` (`full` enables every one), with TipTap's JSON names, commands, and keys:

- `Subscript` (`Mod-,`) and `Superscript` (`Mod-.`), which exclude each other.
- `Highlight`: `==text==`, `Mod-Shift-h`, and a `color` attribute (multicolour by default; `Highlight { multicolor: false }` matches TipTap's default).
- `TextStyle` with `Color`, `BackgroundColor`, `FontFamily`, `FontSize`, and `LineHeight`, which each add one attribute to the `textStyle` mark, with set and unset commands and a query for the shared value.

Supporting changes:

- `canvist_model`: `SchemaBuilder::block_attrs` and `mark_attrs` add attributes to types other extensions register, like TipTap's global attributes. `MarkSpec::excludes_registered` excludes marks only when the schema has them. `EmbedSpec::attrs` sets an embed's defaults.
- `canvist_core`: `commands::update_mark_attrs` rewrites one mark's attributes run by run, keeping each run's others.
- `canvist_layout`: `TextStyle::baseline_shift` and `TextPatch::baseline_shift` raise or lower text like CSS `vertical-align`, in canvas layout and server-rendered HTML alike. `AttrBinding::LineHeight` reads a mark's line height. The StarterKit theme styles `subscript`, `superscript`, and `textStyle.backgroundColor` and `lineHeight`. `TextStyle` has a new public field, so code that builds one literally must set `baseline_shift`.
- Clipboard formats: HTML reads and writes `<sub>`, `<sup>`, `<mark data-color>`, and `<span style>`; Markdown writes `==text==` and GitHub's `<sub>` and `<sup>` tags and reads them back. Pasted marks keep only the attributes their type declares.
- `canvist_headless`: the `full` feature registers every extension by name in `Engine::named`, which `canvist_headless_wasm` and the Dart bridge enable. The browser editor still compiles the StarterKit only. `Engine::named` now registers names in one fixed order whatever order they are given in, so the same names always build the same schema and every binding nests and serializes marks alike.
- `@canvist/headless/full` and the Dart `canvist` package export a typed descriptor and handle for each new extension, generated from the new full metadata snapshot. `allExtensions` (TypeScript) and `Extensions.starterKit` (Dart) list them; `starterKit` is unchanged.
- Conformance fixtures can list `extensions` to add to the StarterKit, and every runner supports them.

The StarterKit theme's rules for blocks, marks, and embeds beyond the StarterKit sit behind a new `canvist_layout` feature, `theme-extensions`. `canvist_canvas`, `canvist_canvas_wasm`, and `canvist_paint` turn it on. `@canvist/web` builds without it, and its bundle budget moves to 352,000 gzipped bytes for the engine growth every host shares.

#### Add `canvist`, a pure Dart package, and rebuild `canvist_flutter` on it

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #113](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/113)

Add `canvist`, a pure Dart package (`platforms/dart`, no Flutter) over `canvist_headless`, and rebuild `canvist_flutter` on top of it.

- The Rust adapter (`canvist_dart`, formerly `canvist_flutter`) binds `canvist_headless` through flutter_rust_bridge and is compiled by the Dart build hook, so `dart run`, `dart test`, and `dart build cli` work on macOS and Linux with the Dart SDK alone. A small loader finds the library through the Dart VM's native-assets mapping, which flutter_rust_bridge's file-name loader cannot.
- `EngineBuilder.add(Extensions.bold)` returns typed handles, generated from the extension metadata, whose methods return typed `Command`s and `Query<T>`s. Engines, documents, formats, UTF-16 positions, snapshots, `CanvistException` with shared `ErrorCode`s, and the Yjs peer and y-sync server API mirror the Rust and TypeScript packages.
- `dart test` passes the shared conformance fixtures (30 of 30), API tests, and an end-to-end test of the `dart:io` example server (Markdown conversion plus a y-websocket endpoint) with two peers over WebSockets. A new `dart` workflow runs them on Linux and macOS without Flutter.
- `canvist_flutter` now depends on and re-exports `canvist`; its example app and integration tests use the real engine instead of the placeholder handle.
- `Engine::named` registers StarterKit extensions by name, shared by the TypeScript and Dart bindings.

#### Add images, YouTube and Twitch videos, audio, and file attachments _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #169](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/169) Five media blocks, each behind its own Cargo feature (`media` enables them all, and `full` includes them). Each is an atomic block whose attributes say what to show. Layout reserves a slot for it, sized by its `height` attribute, and the host draws the picture, player, or file card there: - `Image` (`image`): `setImage` with `src`, `alt`, `title`, `width`, and `height`. Typing `![alt](src "title")` inserts one, even with typography's curly quotes. - `Youtube` (`youtube`) and `Twitch` (`twitch`): `setYoutubeVideo` and `setTwitchVideo`, with TipTap's attributes. As in TipTap, they refuse URLs that are not `http(s)` on YouTube's or Twitch's hosts, so a `javascript:` URL never becomes a frame. - `Audio` (`audio`): `setAudio` with `controls`, `autoplay`, `loop`, and `muted`. - `File` (`file`): Remirror's attachment card, with `insertFile`, `url`, `fileName`, `fileType`, and `fileSize`. All five are data-driven by one implementation. Attributes equal to their default are left out, as everywhere else. - HTML reads and writes TipTap's markup: ``, `

#### Paint ink strokes on iOS, Android, and in Flutter

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #179](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/179)

Display lists now carry ink strokes past the web canvas to the native and Flutter hosts.

- `canvist_ffi` adds `DisplayItem::Stroke` with the stroke's points, width, colour, and bounds. The iOS and Android `DisplayPainter`s draw it as a polyline with round caps and joins.
- `canvist-dart` adds `ViewItemKind.stroke`, with `ViewItem.points` as `x, y` pairs and `ViewItem.lineWidth`. The item's rectangle bounds the points and caps.
- `canvist_flutter`'s `DisplayPainter` draws strokes the same way. A stroke of one point is a dot.

#### Add mentions, hashtags, and emoji on a shared suggestion system

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #166](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/166)

Three extensions, each behind its own Cargo feature and part of `full`, share one suggestion engine, like TipTap's Suggestion utility and Remirror's suggesters. Typing `@`, `#`, or `:` after a space starts a suggestion. A `…Suggestion` query reports `{ char, query }`, a command replaces the trigger with the pick and a space, and Escape or a dismiss command hides it until the trigger is typed again.

- `Mention`: TipTap's `mention` embed with `id`, `label`, and `mentionSuggestionChar`, plus `insertMention`, `dismissMentionSuggestion`, and `mentionSuggestion`. Backspace after a mention turns it back into its trigger.
- `Hashtag`: a `hashtag` mark with a `tag`, marked as you type and paste, with `insertHashtag`, `dismissHashtagSuggestion`, `hashtagSuggestion`, and a `hashtags` list query.
- `Emoji`: TipTap's `emoji` embed with `name`, plus canvist's `emoji` attribute holding the character. It covers GitHub's 1,870 gemoji, `:shortcode:` as you type, `setEmoji`, `dismissEmojiSuggestion`, `emojiSuggestion`, and `searchEmoji({ query, limit })`.

Supporting changes:

- `canvist_model`: `Value::Map` holds nested attributes. JSON objects in attributes become maps instead of `null`, and they round-trip.
- `canvist_core`: `ValueType::List` and `ValueType::Record` describe structured query answers. Bindings generate typed lists and records from them.
- `canvist_collab`: maps in attributes travel through Yjs instead of being dropped.
- `canvist_layout`: `EmbedStyle::Label` gains a `fallback` attribute, drawn when the label's attribute is missing: after the prefix, or as `:value:` without one. The StarterKit theme draws an emoji without its character as `:name:` and a mention without a label as `@id`, as every export does. Code that builds a `Label` literally must set `fallback`.
- `canvist_headless`: query and command arguments accept JSON objects.
- Clipboard: HTML reads and writes TipTap's mention and emoji spans and canvist's hashtag spans. A mention without a label reads back without one. Plain text and Markdown write what a mention or emoji shows.
- `@canvist/headless` types list and record answers. The Dart `canvist` package answers with typed records, such as `({String char, String query})`, and its queries take arguments.

The `@canvist/web` bundle budget moves to 356,000 gzipped bytes and its wasm budget to 342,000, for JSON object and list values and list and record argument types, which every host runs.

The StarterKit theme's mention rule moves behind `canvist_layout`'s `theme-extensions` feature, beside the emoji rule, so hosts that compile only the StarterKit, such as `@canvist/web`, carry neither.

The Dart package's Flutter editor views turn on `canvist_layout`'s `theme-extensions` feature, so they style the extensions the package ships.

#### Add tables

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #177](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/177)

`Table` (feature `table`, included in `full`) is TipTap's TableKit. It adds a `table` of `tableRow`s holding `tableCell`s and `tableHeader`s, each cell holding blocks, with TipTap's `colspan`, `rowspan`, and `colwidth` attributes.

- **Commands:**
  - `insertTable`;
  - `addColumnBefore`, `addColumnAfter`, `deleteColumn`;
  - `addRowBefore`, `addRowAfter`, `deleteRow`;
  - `deleteTable`, `mergeCells`, `splitCell`, `mergeOrSplit`;
  - `toggleHeaderRow`, `toggleHeaderColumn`, `toggleHeaderCell`;
  - `setCellAttribute`, `goToNextCell`, `goToPreviousCell`, `fixTables`.
- **Query:** `tableCell` returns where the selection head sits, with its spans and the table's size.
- **Selections:** a selection from one cell to another selects the rectangle of cells between them.
- **Keys:** Tab moves to the next cell and adds a row past the last. Backspace and Delete never join text across a cell's edge, and deleting a selection across cells clears them.
- **Headers:** toggling the header row or column leaves the corner cell to the other one when it is on, as TipTap does, so toggling twice changes nothing.
- **Repairs:** short rows are padded with empty cells after every structural change, including a gap left of a cell that spans down from the row above.

`canvist_model` adds `TableMap`, which places a table's cells on its grid from their spans.

Layout places tables on a grid:

- Columns take their `colwidth`, or an even share of what is left.
- Each row is as tall as its tallest cell, and spanning cells grow their last row.
- Grid lines are drawn as CSS's collapsed borders.
- Hit testing, arrow keys, incremental relayout, and splicing all follow the grid.
- A keystroke in a table of 1,000 cells relays out in about 7 µs.

The HTML renderer writes a fixed-layout `<table>` with the same column widths, and gives header cells a `scope`: `col` across the first row and `row` down the first column. The StarterKit theme draws hairlines and tints header cells.

HTML reads and writes `<table>` as TipTap does, including bare text in cells and a row that a merged cell spans entirely. Markdown writes a GitHub pipe table when the table fits one exactly, and HTML when it does not. It reads both back, with column alignment.

Grid layout sits behind a new default `canvist_layout` feature, `tables`, which `canvist_canvas`, `canvist_canvas_wasm`, and `canvist_paint` turn on. `canvist_web` builds without it, and the `@canvist/web` bundle budget moves to 357,000 gzipped bytes and its wasm budget to 343,000, for the grid hooks every host carries.

#### Publish the Dart and Flutter packages to pub.dev

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #150](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/150)

The `canvist` package's Rust crate no longer inherits anything from the Cargo workspace. It names `canvist_headless` by the exact crates.io release it was generated against, which monochange bumps on every release, and the workspace's `[patch.crates-io]` builds the local sources inside this repository. So the build hook compiles the crate from the pub cache, where the workspace does not exist.

Both packages now ship a `LICENSE`, a `README.md`, and a repository link, and allow `flutter_rust_bridge` patch releases. CI validates both archives with `pub publish --dry-run` and builds and tests the `canvist` archive outside the repository. The release workflow publishes them after crates.io.

#### Add CanvistEditor, a rich-text editor widget painted from the Rust layout

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #167](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/167)

`canvist_flutter` is now an editor, not just the engine:

- `CanvistEditor` paints canvist's Rust layout with a `DisplayPainter`, measured by `ParagraphMeasurer` with Flutter's own text engine, so lines wrap where Flutter draws them. Only the viewport is laid out, and shaped text runs are cached.
- Input:
  - Text arrives through a delta-model `TextInputClient` that edits the block holding the caret. That covers IME composition, autocorrect, and dictation, and Backspace and Enter from soft keyboards join and split blocks.
  - Hardware keys run the extensions' key bindings.
  - Touch devices get selection handles and the adaptive toolbar.
  - Mouse and trackpad support drag, double click, triple click, shift-click, and a right-click menu.
  - Copy and paste keep formatting within the editor.
- Undo and redo, scrolling that keeps the caret in view, accessibility semantics (text field value, selection, and actions), dark mode, and text scaling. Assistive technology and UI automation that set the field's whole text get the smallest edit, so formatting survives.
- `CanvistController` holds the document and runs typed commands and queries from the engine's handles. It applies Yjs updates and y-sync messages, notifying listeners on every change. `CanvistController.keyPlatform` makes `Mod` Cmd on Apple devices.
- `CanvistStyle` and `CanvistFonts` choose fonts, size, and line height.
- The example app is a full editor with a formatting toolbar and a two-peer collaboration demo.
- Tests:
  - Widget tests cover text input, IME, keys, mouse and touch selection, the toolbar, scrolling, semantics, collaboration, and fast typing.
  - Golden tests compare the editor's layout and pixels with server rendering, both from the painter and from the live widget.
  - Integration tests run on the iOS Simulator and an Android emulator.
  - Patrol tests drive the example app through the device: the platform keyboard, native taps and swipes, long presses, the toolbar, two peers, and system dark mode. They also compare the editor's on-device pixels with server rendering.
  - Keystroke-to-frame budgets run on the host and on devices.

sections.title: 🐛 Fixed
entries:
- **Stop restarting Android keyboards while the editor has focus.** Android keyboards mark the word at the caret when their input starts, for suggestions. `CanvistEditor` sent its own state back without that mark, which made Android restart the keyboard, which marked the word again, several times a second for as long as the editor had focus. The keyboard and its suggestion strip churned, and suggestions and autocorrect kept resetting. The editor now leaves the word the keyboard marks alone, and composing over it works as before.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #187](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/187)

#### Publish the Dart and Flutter packages to pub.dev

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #150](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/150)

The `canvist` package's Rust crate no longer inherits anything from the Cargo workspace. It names `canvist_headless` by the exact crates.io release it was generated against, which monochange bumps on every release, and the workspace's `[patch.crates-io]` builds the local sources inside this repository. So the build hook compiles the crate from the pub cache, where the workspace does not exist.

Both packages now ship a `LICENSE`, a `README.md`, and a repository link, and allow `flutter_rust_bridge` patch releases. CI validates both archives with `pub publish --dry-run` and builds and tests the `canvist` archive outside the repository. The release workflow publishes them after crates.io.

- **Keep a selection the app sets while the keyboard is still starting.** A keyboard's first updates after the editor gains focus describe the caret the editor opened with. When an app set a new selection in that moment, for example selecting everything as the editor opens, those late updates arrived after it and collapsed the selection, so the next format applied to nothing. `CanvistEditor` now recognises an update that only returns to a selection it has since replaced, and keeps its own.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #195](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/195)

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #150](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/150)

The `canvist` package's Rust crate no longer inherits anything from the Cargo workspace. It names `canvist_headless` by the exact crates.io release it was generated against, which monochange bumps on every release, and the workspace's `[patch.crates-io]` builds the local sources inside this repository. So the build hook compiles the crate from the pub cache, where the workspace does not exist.

Both packages now ship a `LICENSE`, a `README.md`, and a repository link, and allow `flutter_rust_bridge` patch releases. CI validates both archives with `pub publish --dry-run` and builds and tests the `canvist` archive outside the repository. The release workflow publishes them after crates.io.

- **Keep a selection the app sets while the keyboard is still starting.** A keyboard's first updates after the editor gains focus describe the caret the editor opened with. When an app set a new selection in that moment, for example selecting everything as the editor opens, those late updates arrived after it and collapsed the selection, so the next format applied to nothing. `CanvistEditor` now recognises an update that only returns to a selection it has since replaced, and keeps its own.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #195](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/195)

sections.title: 🚀 Feature
entries:
- **Sell annual Builder and Scale plans self-serve.** `POST /v1/billing/checkout` now takes `"interval": "year"` (monthly stays the default). An annual plan bills its base fee yearly and its overage monthly, which Stripe Checkout cannot create, so the annual Checkout page saves a card and the Stripe webhook creates the subscription in flexible billing mode, anchored to the first of the month. A retried or repeated webhook never creates a second subscription, and `POST /v1/billing/plan` keeps an annual subscription annual when it switches between Builder and Scale.
  _Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #142](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/142)

- **Bill canvist Cloud through a durable usage outbox, Checkout, and the Customer Portal.** Bill canvist Cloud the way Stripe recommends. Usage is reported through a durable Postgres outbox, so restarts and Stripe outages delay it without losing it, and conversions are now billed on the `canvist_conversion` meter as aggregated counts. Subscriptions start with `POST /v1/billing/checkout`, anchored to the first of the month so Stripe's billing periods match monthly active documents; `POST /v1/billing/plan` switches between Builder and Scale; and `POST /v1/billing/portal` opens the Customer Portal. The webhook now handles checkout and invoice events and applies each subscription's current state, so out-of-order events and old subscriptions cannot change a project's plan, and a failed payment keeps the plan while Stripe retries. The setup script adds product tax codes, tax-exclusive prices, the Customer Portal configuration, and a Stripe Tax readiness check. See `docs/src/cloud/stripe-plan.md`.
  _Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #122](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/122)

- **Add canvist Convert between ProseMirror JSON, HTML, Markdown, and text.** Add canvist Convert to `canvist_cloud`: `POST /v1/convert` turns documents between ProseMirror JSON, HTML, Markdown, and plain text on `canvist_headless` with the StarterKit, and `GET /v1/documents/{name}?format=…` exports a synced document in any of them. Conversions run on the blocking pool under a size limit, a timeout, and a concurrency bound, and count toward the month's usage. `CANVIST_ROLE=convert` serves only these routes, so Convert scales as its own service from the same image.
  _Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #118](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/118)

#### Count monthly active documents (MADs) and enforce plans

_Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #117](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/117)

- A document is active in a month once a sync session opens it or the REST API writes it, counted once per project environment and month in a `usage` table. `GET /v1/usage` reports it against the plan as `ok`, `approaching`, `over`, or `capped`.
- The free plan's cap pauses only sessions on documents new this month: the socket stays open, the client keeps editing locally, documents already active keep syncing, and a paused session syncs on its own after an upgrade. Admissions take a per-project lock, so concurrent sessions cannot overshoot the cap.
- Paid plans warn and never pause. New paid documents send one Stripe Billing Meter event each, test-mode keys only, with deterministic identifiers.

- **Stop echoing carets and batch persistence in canvist Sync.** A client's own caret is no longer echoed back to it, which was a third of a typing client's traffic; quiet sockets get a keepalive instead, so clients never hit their reconnect timeout. Each flush now writes every edited document in one transaction of two statements, so Postgres sees four writes a second however many documents are open: 1,000 edited documents flush in 20 ms, down from 155 ms. Adds a live load test (`services/cloud/tests/js/load.ts`), and the smoke and load tests no longer let same-process clients bypass the relay over `BroadcastChannel`.
  _Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #129](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/129)

- **Turn Stripe subscription events into project plans.** Close the billing loop with Stripe: `POST /v1/stripe/webhook` verifies Stripe's signature and turns subscription events into project plans, so an upgrade unpauses a full free plan on its own. Add `services/cloud/stripe/setup.ts` (`deno task stripe:setup`), an idempotent, test-mode-only script that creates the Billing Meters, products, prices, and webhook endpoint for the provisional plans, and document billing in `docs/src/cloud/billing.md`.
  _Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #121](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/121)

#### Add `canvist_cloud`, starting with Sync: a multi-tenant y-sync relay

_Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #116](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/116)

- Stock `y-websocket` and Hocuspocus clients connect to `/v1/sync/{document}` and `/v1/hocuspocus`, with presence, read-only sessions, and per-document access from short-lived HS256 tokens that API keys mint.
- Documents persist to Postgres as merged Yjs updates, compact into snapshots, and leave memory once idle. Updates that write outside the `blocks` root or put bare values in it are refused.
- Debounced, signed `document.updated` webhooks; REST endpoints to list, read, write, and delete documents; health and readiness probes; and a graceful shutdown that persists every room.
- `canvist_collab::Reorder` is now public, so hosts with a bare yrs document apply out-of-order updates safely.

#### Add the canvist website, deployed to Railway

_Packages:_ 🟠 _website_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #115](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/115)

Add canvist's website in `website/`: an Astro site with the landing page, preview pricing with a monthly-active-document calculator, the Sync, Convert and History service pages, and a `/docs` section that renders `docs/src` with Pagefind search.

- The landing page is a "fan deck" of Paint swatches that fans open as you scroll. The hero's Wet Caret paints the wordmark in Rive (`website/rive/`, generated from the brand masters). The page also has the engine typing live with a keystroke-to-paint readout, one document morphing across seven hosts, simulated multiplayer carets, a TypeScript error that lights up when an extension is missing, and benchmark bars read from the architecture doc's budget table at build time.
- Every animation has a reduced-motion state, and GSAP, Rive and the wasm engine never load under reduced motion.
- The site deploys to Railway as the `website` service, built from `website/Dockerfile` at the repository root and served by Caddy.
- A new `website` CI workflow runs the type check, unit tests, the build, Playwright (navigation, reduced motion, responsiveness at 320, 768, 1280 and 1920 px, and axe accessibility checks) and Lighthouse CI. A macOS job compares visual snapshots.

- **Add the /changelog page for app releases.** `/changelog` renders the `changelog` collection (the user release stream monochange writes into `website/src/content/changelog/`), newest version first, with a linkable heading per release and an empty state until the first app release. The footer links to it, and the page joins the end-to-end sweeps (navigation, responsiveness and accessibility in both themes).
  _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #127](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/127)

#### Type in previews, edit every extension in the playground, and see collaborators' cursors

_Packages:_ 🟠 _website_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #235](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/235)

- A docs sample's preview is the editor itself, and people can type in it: the HTML, JSON, and Markdown tabs follow their edits until the code runs again. Documents with extensions beyond the StarterKit load `@canvist/web/full`, so every sample gets an editor.
- In the playground, the Every extension document is an editor with all 49 extensions, and switching on an extension beyond the StarterKit in the Editor example moves its import to `@canvist/web/full` instead of being unavailable.
- The Collaboration example shows each peer's caret, with a name tag in the peer's colour, in every other peer's editor. Its server relays presence over a second socket, and each peer frame learns its name and colour from its URL.
- "Add a peer" only shows for examples with a server, since peers without one share nothing, and a new peer scrolls into view.

#### Embed the web editor on the landing page

_Packages:_ 🟠 _website_

The "Type into the real engine" demo now runs `@canvist/web`, the editor canvist ships.

- The page arrives with the demo's document as HTML, rendered at build time by `@canvist/headless/ssr` with the page's own Bricolage and Geist Mono faces. The editor hydrates from it and swaps in the canvas in one frame, with no layout shift. Visitors without JavaScript, and crawlers, see the text.
- The editor still loads only once the section is on screen and scrolling has settled. Under reduced motion or Save-Data it loads when the visitor presses the document or the button. Starting it leaves focus and the scroll position where they were.
- The sheet follows the site's light and dark themes, and the theme toggle recreates the editor in the other scheme, keeping the document, selection, and focus.
- The readout's values have room for "123.4 ms", so new numbers no longer move the labels.
- The website build compiles `@canvist/headless` and `@canvist/web` from the workspace, in a `packages` CI job and a Rust stage in `website/Dockerfile`.

#### Run the docs' samples on the page, and add a playground

_Packages:_ 🟠 _website_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #234](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/234)

- Every runnable TypeScript sample in the docs, and the browser samples marked `live` (`ts no_run live`), gets a **Run** button. It turns the sample into an editor that reruns as it changes, shows what it printed (and whether that matches the comments `docs/check-snippets.ts` checks), and previews the document it made: painted by `@canvist/web` when it only uses the StarterKit, and as HTML, JSON, and Markdown.
- `/playground` runs examples with server code and browser code: the editor with a toolbar built from its extensions, a document using all 49 extensions, a collaboration server with live peers, and a `node:http` server. A switch for every extension rewrites the code's extension list and import.
- The sandbox (`website/src/sandbox`) runs server code in a worker with `@canvist/headless` (and `/full`, `/ssr`), `ws`, `node:http`, `node:events`, `Deno.serve`, `process`, and `Buffer`, on a `localhost` that only the tab can reach. Browser code runs in frames whose `WebSocket` and `fetch` to `localhost` reach that worker. Code only comes from the page itself, never a URL.
- Agents script the playground through `window.canvistPlayground`, documented in the agents guide.

#### Redesign the landing page for clarity and smooth motion

_Packages:_ 🟠 _website_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #126](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/126)

- The landing page has six beats with one idea each: the hero, the live editor, one document on every platform, writing together, free forever plus the services, and the call to action. Benchmarks, the platform matrix and API samples now live in the docs.
- Motion is CSS transitions on `transform` and `opacity` only, with one easing. Nothing is pinned or scroll-linked, and GSAP is gone. Scrolling stays inside one 60 Hz frame with no long tasks, even with the CPU throttled 4×.
- Nothing is cut off at any common screen size. A new Playwright check scrolls every page across nine viewports and fails on clipped content or horizontal overflow. Visual snapshots cover each viewport's first screen.
- The live editor no longer steals keyboard focus when it loads, and starts only while its section is on screen and scrolling has paused.

sections.title: 📝 Changed
entries:
- **Move the repository to canvist/canvist.** canvist now lives at [github.com/canvist/canvist](https://github.com/canvist/canvist). Every repository, documentation, and badge link points there, the npm packages declare their repository, homepage, and issue tracker (with support@canvist.dev), and the release workflows run for the `canvist` organisation. The website footer has a Contact link to support@canvist.dev.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_, 🟠 _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #148](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/148)

- **Show every package readme in the docs, without its GitHub header.** The docs' Packages section now includes `@canvist/web`, `@canvist/react`, `@canvist/vue`, `@canvist/headless`, and `@canvist/canvas`, whose lowercase `readme.md` files the loader used to miss on case-sensitive file systems. Readmes open with a centred logo, links, and badges for GitHub and the registries; the site drops that whole header, since its own page header already carries the logo.
  _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #147](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/147)

- **Run Lighthouse on mobile too and report scores in CI.** The website's CI runs Lighthouse with both the desktop preset and the mobile profile, and writes a median-per-page score table to every run's summary. Desktop must reach 95+ in every category, LCP under 1.5 s and CLS 0. Mobile must reach the same scores and CLS 0, and reports LCP over 1.5 s as a warning. The docs search hint no longer shifts layout.
  _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #124](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/124)

sections.title: 🐛 Fixed
entries:
- **Bound conversion admission before reading input.** Reserve conversion capacity before reading JSON request bodies or loading stored documents for export. When every slot is occupied, return `503` with code `converter_unavailable` immediately instead of retaining inputs in an unbounded semaphore queue. Cancelled uploads and rejected inputs release their slots, while timed-out blocking work retains capacity until it finishes.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #223](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/223)

- **Deploy canvist Cloud on Railway as the sync and convert services.** Deploy canvist Cloud on Railway: a multi-stage Dockerfile (`services/cloud/Dockerfile`) producing a Debian slim image with only the `canvist-cloud` binary, run as the `sync` and `convert` services of the `canvist` project in `production` and `staging`. Add a live smoke test (`services/cloud/tests/js/smoke.ts`) that syncs real Yjs clients through a deployment, and document the deployment, its variables, and its measured cost per thousand monthly active documents.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #119](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/119)

- **Bound updates waiting for missing dependencies.** Count retained Yjs submissions toward the document byte limit, including updates pending inside yrs, and cap unresolved batches at 128 distinct submissions per room. Identical replays are deduplicated before decoding and readiness scans. Release the retained-input charges when dependencies resolve and both buffers drain.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #226](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/226)

- **Prevent webhook DNS resolution from reaching private networks.** Check DNS answers when configuring webhooks and on every new delivery connection. Reject private or mixed address sets, keep the checked addresses for the connection, and disable proxy and redirect bypasses. Stored webhook URLs are rechecked before delivery. Self-hosters can still explicitly enable private destinations.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #221](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/221)

#### Fix three ways collaborating peers' documents could diverge

_Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #135](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/135)

- A block copy that loses its id to a concurrently moved copy is now evicted from where it sits in the shared array, not from its old place in the model. Blocks inserted after it in the same update used to land out of order on the receiving peer.
- A hidden copy of a block, such as one inside a list that no longer allows it, no longer claims the block's id when reading a document from scratch. `Binding::document` used to hide the shown copy and delete it from the shared document.
- `Reorder::take_ready` is replaced by `Reorder::take_next`, which releases one update at a time against the document's current state vector. An update that yrs keeps pending, because it is inserted next to another client's item that has not arrived, no longer lets that client's later updates overtake it. The binding and canvist Sync rooms both apply updates this way.

- **Update rustls-webpki to 0.103.16.** canvist Cloud verifies TLS certificates with rustls-webpki, which 0.103.16 patches for RUSTSEC-2026-0382.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #158](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/158)

- **Enforce sync token expiry throughout a connection.** Close live and paused sync connections when their client tokens expire. Validate every Hocuspocus token refresh and replace its scope and lifetime, closing expired sockets with code 1008.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #225](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/225)

- **The image build relinks after copying the site in.** Follow-up to the release pull request workspace builds: the image's deno stage installed from a relinked manifest and then copied the checked-in website over it, restoring dependency ranges that npm cannot resolve yet on a release commit. The relink now runs again after the copy.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #228](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/228)

- **Release pull requests build the site from workspace packages.** Release preparation rewrites internal dependencies to ranges (`^0.2.0`) that name versions npm will only have after the release publishes. A relink step now runs before every website and bundle-size deno resolution — including the website image build — repointing those ranges at the workspace packages, so release pull requests pass CI and the site keeps building from local artifacts.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #227](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/227)

- **Show iOS, Android, and Flutter as available on the landing page.** The landing page's platform list now marks iOS (UIKit and SwiftUI), Android (Views and Jetpack Compose), and Flutter as available, matching the docs, and says "coming soon" for React Native and Lynx instead of internal milestone codes.
  _Packages:_ 🟢 _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #197](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/197)

sections.title: 📖 Documentation
entries:
#### Rewrite the docs for people and agents using canvist

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #130](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/130)

- New structure: get started (one quick start per platform, each marked available, preview, or coming soon), core concepts, an extension catalogue, a build-your-own-editor guide, guides, an AI agent guide, canvist Cloud, and reference.
- Every Rust, TypeScript, and Dart sample runs in CI: Rust pages are doc tests of `canvist_book`, and `docs/check-snippets.ts` type-checks, analyzes, and runs the others, checking printed output against the comments.
- The website serves `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`, and groups the docs sidebar by `SUMMARY.md` parts. A draft `canvist` agent skill lives in `skills/canvist/`.
- Design records, research, the roadmap, and canvist Cloud operations move to `docs/internal/`, outside the published docs.

- **Order the integrations by ecosystem popularity.** The docs sidebar, the platform tables, the agent guide, and `/llms.txt` now list integrations by expected usage: the TypeScript ecosystem first (React, React Native, Vue, web, server-side rendering, the TypeScript server, and the design canvas), then Flutter with the Dart server, iOS, Android, desktop with the Rust server, and Lynx last.
  _Packages:_ ⚪ _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #209](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/209)

#### Document React Native and Lynx, and list them as previews

_Packages:_ ⚪ _website_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #199](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/199)

- New quick starts for [React Native](docs/src/quick-start/react-native.md) and [Lynx](docs/src/quick-start/lynx.md): install from the repository, show an editor, add a toolbar that follows the selection, save and load, and what calls from JavaScript cost.
- The platform tables in the README and the quick-start index, the website's platforms section, and the agent notes in `/llms.txt` list React Native and Lynx as previews, installed from GitHub.
- The agent guide and the `canvist` skill list React Native and Lynx, and the skill the iOS, Android, and desktop editors, among the packages that exist.

- **Mark the browser platforms Available.** The web, React, Vue, server-side rendering, and design canvas quick starts, the platform tables in the readme and the docs, the agent guide and skill, and the website's platform list now say "Available". The package readmes describe read-only editors, placeholders, menus, collaboration, server rendering, and the bundle budget.
  _Packages:_ ⚪ _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #173](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/173)

- **List the desktop editor as available on the site and in llms.txt.** The platforms section shows Desktop as available on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and the agent notes in `/llms.txt` name `canvist_desktop` among the packages that work today.
  _Packages:_ ⚪ _website_
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #163](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/163)
