Add `services/cloud/stripe/setup.ts` (`deno task stripe:setup`), an idempotent, test-mode-only script that creates the Billing Meters, products, prices, and webhook endpoint for the provisional plans, and document billing in `docs/src/cloud/billing.md`. _Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #121](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/121) #### Add `canvist_cloud`, starting with Sync: a multi-tenant y-sync relay _Packages:_ 🟠 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #116](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/116) - Stock `y-websocket` and Hocuspocus clients connect to `/v1/sync/{document}` and `/v1/hocuspocus`, with presence, read-only sessions, and per-document access from short-lived HS256 tokens that API keys mint. - Documents persist to Postgres as merged Yjs updates, compact into snapshots, and leave memory once idle. Updates that write outside the `blocks` root or put bare values in it are refused. - Debounced, signed `document.updated` webhooks; REST endpoints to list, read, write, and delete documents; health and readiness probes; and a graceful shutdown that persists every room. - `canvist_collab::Reorder` is now public, so hosts with a bare yrs document apply out-of-order updates safely. #### Add the canvist website, deployed to Railway _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #115](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/115) Add canvist's website in `website/`: an Astro site with the landing page, preview pricing with a monthly-active-document calculator, the Sync, Convert and History service pages, and a `/docs` section that renders `docs/src` with Pagefind search. - The landing page is a "fan deck" of Paint swatches that fans open as you scroll. The hero's Wet Caret paints the wordmark in Rive (`website/rive/`, generated from the brand masters). The page also has the engine typing live with a keystroke-to-paint readout, one document morphing across seven hosts, simulated multiplayer carets, a TypeScript error that lights up when an extension is missing, and benchmark bars read from the architecture doc's budget table at build time. - Every animation has a reduced-motion state, and GSAP, Rive and the wasm engine never load under reduced motion. - The site deploys to Railway as the `website` service, built from `website/Dockerfile` at the repository root and served by Caddy. - A new `website` CI workflow runs the type check, unit tests, the build, Playwright (navigation, reduced motion, responsiveness at 320, 768, 1280 and 1920 px, and axe accessibility checks) and Lighthouse CI. A macOS job compares visual snapshots. - **Add the /changelog page for app releases.** `/changelog` renders the `changelog` collection (the user release stream monochange writes into `website/src/content/changelog/`), newest version first, with a linkable heading per release and an empty state until the first app release. The footer links to it, and the page joins the end-to-end sweeps (navigation, responsiveness and accessibility in both themes). _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #127](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/127) #### Type in previews, edit every extension in the playground, and see collaborators' cursors _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #235](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/235) - A docs sample's preview is the editor itself, and people can type in it: the HTML, JSON, and Markdown tabs follow their edits until the code runs again. Documents with extensions beyond the StarterKit load `@canvist/web/full`, so every sample gets an editor. - In the playground, the Every extension document is an editor with all 49 extensions, and switching on an extension beyond the StarterKit in the Editor example moves its import to `@canvist/web/full` instead of being unavailable. - The Collaboration example shows each peer's caret, with a name tag in the peer's colour, in every other peer's editor. Its server relays presence over a second socket, and each peer frame learns its name and colour from its URL. - "Add a peer" only shows for examples with a server, since peers without one share nothing, and a new peer scrolls into view. #### Embed the web editor on the landing page _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_ The "Type into the real engine" demo now runs `@canvist/web`, the editor canvist ships. - The page arrives with the demo's document as HTML, rendered at build time by `@canvist/headless/ssr` with the page's own Bricolage and Geist Mono faces. The editor hydrates from it and swaps in the canvas in one frame, with no layout shift. Visitors without JavaScript, and crawlers, see the text. - The editor still loads only once the section is on screen and scrolling has settled. Under reduced motion or Save-Data it loads when the visitor presses the document or the button. Starting it leaves focus and the scroll position where they were. - The sheet follows the site's light and dark themes, and the theme toggle recreates the editor in the other scheme, keeping the document, selection, and focus. - The readout's values have room for "123.4 ms", so new numbers no longer move the labels. - The website build compiles `@canvist/headless` and `@canvist/web` from the workspace, in a `packages` CI job and a Rust stage in `website/Dockerfile`. #### Run the docs' samples on the page, and add a playground _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #234](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/234) - Every runnable TypeScript sample in the docs, and the browser samples marked `live` (`ts no_run live`), gets a **Run** button. It turns the sample into an editor that reruns as it changes, shows what it printed (and whether that matches the comments `docs/check-snippets.ts` checks), and previews the document it made: painted by `@canvist/web` when it only uses the StarterKit, and as HTML, JSON, and Markdown. - `/playground` runs examples with server code and browser code: the editor with a toolbar built from its extensions, a document using all 49 extensions, a collaboration server with live peers, and a `node:http` server. A switch for every extension rewrites the code's extension list and import. - The sandbox (`website/src/sandbox`) runs server code in a worker with `@canvist/headless` (and `/full`, `/ssr`), `ws`, `node:http`, `node:events`, `Deno.serve`, `process`, and `Buffer`, on a `localhost` that only the tab can reach. Browser code runs in frames whose `WebSocket` and `fetch` to `localhost` reach that worker. Code only comes from the page itself, never a URL. - Agents script the playground through `window.canvistPlayground`, documented in the agents guide. #### Redesign the landing page for clarity and smooth motion _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #126](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/126) - The landing page has six beats with one idea each: the hero, the live editor, one document on every platform, writing together, free forever plus the services, and the call to action. Benchmarks, the platform matrix and API samples now live in the docs. - Motion is CSS transitions on `transform` and `opacity` only, with one easing. Nothing is pinned or scroll-linked, and GSAP is gone. Scrolling stays inside one 60 Hz frame with no long tasks, even with the CPU throttled 4×. - Nothing is cut off at any common screen size. A new Playwright check scrolls every page across nine viewports and fails on clipped content or horizontal overflow. Visual snapshots cover each viewport's first screen. - The live editor no longer steals keyboard focus when it loads, and starts only while its section is on screen and scrolling has paused. ### 📝 Changed - **Move the repository to canvist/canvist.** canvist now lives at [github.com/canvist/canvist](https://github.com/canvist/canvist). Every repository, documentation, and badge link points there, the npm packages declare their repository, homepage, and issue tracker (with support@canvist.dev), and the release workflows run for the `canvist` organisation. The website footer has a Contact link to support@canvist.dev. _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_, 🟠 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #148](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/148) - **Show every package readme in the docs, without its GitHub header.** The docs' Packages section now includes `@canvist/web`, `@canvist/react`, `@canvist/vue`, `@canvist/headless`, and `@canvist/canvas`, whose lowercase `readme.md` files the loader used to miss on case-sensitive file systems. Readmes open with a centred logo, links, and badges for GitHub and the registries; the site drops that whole header, since its own page header already carries the logo. _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #147](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/147) - **Run Lighthouse on mobile too and report scores in CI.** The website's CI runs Lighthouse with both the desktop preset and the mobile profile, and writes a median-per-page score table to every run's summary. Desktop must reach 95+ in every category, LCP under 1.5 s and CLS 0. Mobile must reach the same scores and CLS 0, and reports LCP over 1.5 s as a warning. The docs search hint no longer shifts layout. _Packages:_ 🟠 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #124](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/124) ### 🐛 Fixed - **Bound conversion admission before reading input.** Reserve conversion capacity before reading JSON request bodies or loading stored documents for export. When every slot is occupied, return `503` with code `converter_unavailable` immediately instead of retaining inputs in an unbounded semaphore queue. Cancelled uploads and rejected inputs release their slots, while timed-out blocking work retains capacity until it finishes. _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #223](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/223) - **Deploy canvist Cloud on Railway as the sync and convert services.** Deploy canvist Cloud on Railway: a multi-stage Dockerfile (`services/cloud/Dockerfile`) producing a Debian slim image with only the `canvist-cloud` binary, run as the `sync` and `convert` services of the `canvist` project in `production` and `staging`. Add a live smoke test (`services/cloud/tests/js/smoke.ts`) that syncs real Yjs clients through a deployment, and document the deployment, its variables, and its measured cost per thousand monthly active documents. _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #119](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/119) - **Bound updates waiting for missing dependencies.** Count retained Yjs submissions toward the document byte limit, including updates pending inside yrs, and cap unresolved batches at 128 distinct submissions per room. Identical replays are deduplicated before decoding and readiness scans. Release the retained-input charges when dependencies resolve and both buffers drain. _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #226](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/226) - **Prevent webhook DNS resolution from reaching private networks.** Check DNS answers when configuring webhooks and on every new delivery connection. Reject private or mixed address sets, keep the checked addresses for the connection, and disable proxy and redirect bypasses. Stored webhook URLs are rechecked before delivery. Self-hosters can still explicitly enable private destinations. _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #221](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/221) #### Fix three ways collaborating peers' documents could diverge _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #135](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/135) - A block copy that loses its id to a concurrently moved copy is now evicted from where it sits in the shared array, not from its old place in the model. Blocks inserted after it in the same update used to land out of order on the receiving peer. - A hidden copy of a block, such as one inside a list that no longer allows it, no longer claims the block's id when reading a document from scratch. `Binding::document` used to hide the shown copy and delete it from the shared document. - `Reorder::take_ready` is replaced by `Reorder::take_next`, which releases one update at a time against the document's current state vector. An update that yrs keeps pending, because it is inserted next to another client's item that has not arrived, no longer lets that client's later updates overtake it. The binding and canvist Sync rooms both apply updates this way. - **Update rustls-webpki to 0.103.16.** canvist Cloud verifies TLS certificates with rustls-webpki, which 0.103.16 patches for RUSTSEC-2026-0382. _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #158](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/158) - **Enforce sync token expiry throughout a connection.** Close live and paused sync connections when their client tokens expire. Validate every Hocuspocus token refresh and replace its scope and lifetime, closing expired sockets with code 1008. _Packages:_ 🟢 _canvist_cloud_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #225](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/225) - **The image build relinks after copying the site in.** Follow-up to the release pull request workspace builds: the image's deno stage installed from a relinked manifest and then copied the checked-in website over it, restoring dependency ranges that npm cannot resolve yet on a release commit. The relink now runs again after the copy. _Packages:_ 🟢 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #228](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/228) - **Release pull requests build the site from workspace packages.** Release preparation rewrites internal dependencies to ranges (`^0.2.0`) that name versions npm will only have after the release publishes. A relink step now runs before every website and bundle-size deno resolution — including the website image build — repointing those ranges at the workspace packages, so release pull requests pass CI and the site keeps building from local artifacts. _Packages:_ 🟢 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #227](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/227) - **Show iOS, Android, and Flutter as available on the landing page.** The landing page's platform list now marks iOS (UIKit and SwiftUI), Android (Views and Jetpack Compose), and Flutter as available, matching the docs, and says "coming soon" for React Native and Lynx instead of internal milestone codes. _Packages:_ 🟢 _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #197](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/197)
📖 Documentation #### Rewrite the docs for people and agents using canvist _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #130](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/130) - New structure: get started (one quick start per platform, each marked available, preview, or coming soon), core concepts, an extension catalogue, a build-your-own-editor guide, guides, an AI agent guide, canvist Cloud, and reference. - Every Rust, TypeScript, and Dart sample runs in CI: Rust pages are doc tests of `canvist_book`, and `docs/check-snippets.ts` type-checks, analyzes, and runs the others, checking printed output against the comments. - The website serves `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`, and groups the docs sidebar by `SUMMARY.md` parts. A draft `canvist` agent skill lives in `skills/canvist/`. - Design records, research, the roadmap, and canvist Cloud operations move to `docs/internal/`, outside the published docs. - **Order the integrations by ecosystem popularity.** The docs sidebar, the platform tables, the agent guide, and `/llms.txt` now list integrations by expected usage: the TypeScript ecosystem first (React, React Native, Vue, web, server-side rendering, the TypeScript server, and the design canvas), then Flutter with the Dart server, iOS, Android, desktop with the Rust server, and Lynx last. _Packages:_ ⚪ _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #209](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/209) #### Document React Native and Lynx, and list them as previews _Packages:_ ⚪ _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #199](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/199) - New quick starts for [React Native](docs/src/quick-start/react-native.md) and [Lynx](docs/src/quick-start/lynx.md): install from the repository, show an editor, add a toolbar that follows the selection, save and load, and what calls from JavaScript cost. - The platform tables in the README and the quick-start index, the website's platforms section, and the agent notes in `/llms.txt` list React Native and Lynx as previews, installed from GitHub. - The agent guide and the `canvist` skill list React Native and Lynx, and the skill the iOS, Android, and desktop editors, among the packages that exist. - **Mark the browser platforms Available.** The web, React, Vue, server-side rendering, and design canvas quick starts, the platform tables in the readme and the docs, the agent guide and skill, and the website's platform list now say "Available". The package readmes describe read-only editors, placeholders, menus, collaboration, server rendering, and the bundle budget. _Packages:_ ⚪ _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #173](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/173) - **List the desktop editor as available on the site and in llms.txt.** The platforms section shows Desktop as available on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and the agent notes in `/llms.txt` name `canvist_desktop` among the packages that work today. _Packages:_ ⚪ _website_ _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #163](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/163)

entries:
#### A calmer, smoother canvist website

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #126](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/126)

##### User impact

The canvist home page is shorter and easier to read, scrolls smoothly on every device, and no longer cuts off content on smaller screens.

sections.title: New
entries:
#### canvist runs in React Native and Lynx apps

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #199](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/199)

##### User impact

Apps built with React Native or Lynx can now add canvist's editor. It is the same native editor as on iOS and Android, so typing, autocorrect, dictation, selection, and screen readers work as people expect, not like a web page squeezed into an app. Both are previews for now: they install from GitHub rather than npm.

#### See what's new on the changelog page

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #127](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/127)

##### User impact

The website has a changelog listing new features, fixes and pricing changes on the website and canvist Cloud, newest first. You can find it in the footer.

#### Type in the docs' previews and see who's editing

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #235](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/235)

##### User impact

When you run a sample in the docs, the document it makes opens in a real editor you can type in, whichever extensions it uses. In the playground, the Every extension document is editable too, and in the Collaboration example each person's cursor shows in the other editors with their name, so you can watch someone type.

#### The canvist website is live

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #125](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/125)

##### User impact

You can now see what canvist is and try the editor in your browser. The pricing page estimates your monthly bill from the number of documents you edit each month. The documentation has built-in search. Every animation respects your reduced-motion setting.

#### Try canvist in your browser

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #234](https://github.com/canvist/canvist/pull/234)

##### User impact

Code samples in the docs have a Run button: edit them and see what they print and the document they make. The new playground lets you switch any of canvist's extensions on and off, and runs a collaboration server and several live editors in the same browser tab, with nothing to install.
